title: Bankers are shoring up their defenses against rogue agents
summary:
'Twas the week of big bank earnings, and Wall Street had a new threat on its mind: rogue AI.
Executives at the country's largest financial institutions used their earnings calls to assure investors that they are doing everything in their power to fend off attacks from powerful, rogue AI models.
Later in the call, she said that Citigroup was continuing to "invest in leading-edge capabilities" to strengthen its cyber defenses.
Rogue AI agents are top of mindThe comments from the finance executives come as rogue AI agents by labs like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta, capable of exploiting software vulnerabilities, have hacked into the software and website of several organizations in recent months.
More recently, its agents hacked into Australia's government website , leading Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to express Australia's "extreme concern" about the incident to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

title: Volvo will use Nvidia’s tech for hands-free, point-to-point driving
summary:
Volvo plans to launch hands-free, point-to-point driving by 2030, powered by Nvidia’s latest AI technology.
The Chinese-owned, Swedish-designed automaker said Thursday it would use Nvidia’s autonomous driving stack to power a new partially automated driving system similar to Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (Supervised).
Volvo says the new point-to-point system will be Level 2++, meaning it can handle complex urban environments, including traffic lights, stop signs, and unprotected left turns without explicit driver control.
The automaker had to effectively sideline its Ride Pilot Level 3 unsupervised autonomous driving system in the US after failing to obtain regulatory approval.
Volvo plans to make the new point-to-point driving system available across its vehicle lineup, from entry-level to high-end versions — though the company didn’t reveal which models will come first.

title: Norrsken and Nvidia to open Stockholm AI Lab for founders in 2027
summary:
Norrsken Foundation and Nvidia will open a hub for AI startups in central Stockholm in 2027.
The Stockholm AI Lab will host a select group of European founders who use AI to address problems in climate, health, food and society, and it will also be home to Nvidia’s Stockholm office.
The project follows a pledge Norrsken made in June 2025, when it set aside a €300M AI fund for European startups using AI for social and environmental good.
Earlier this week, chief executive Jensen Huang said the company would put a further $2bn into European AI companies.
Besides Stockholm, Norrsken runs houses in Barcelona, Kigali, Brussels and Amsterdam, and its five funds have raised more than $1bn.

title: An AI CEO is calling out the people who bash AI but can't stop using it
summary:
Beschloss said critics of AI and the data centers that power it aren't above using the technology.
"All the people that are saying they're anti-data center, that they're anti-AI in general, they're using it," Beschloss said on Wednesday during CNBC's Trading the Midterms event.
He said that when people have to choose between shutting down data centers or shutting down ChatGPT, it won't be an easy decision.
His company, Verb, is a data exchange where users can get paid by selling their proprietary information to data-hungry AI companies.
Supporters say building more data centers will create new jobs, bolster economies, and strengthen the country's national security.

title: OpenAI’s CFO says firms using Chinese AI models are risking security
summary:
OpenAI chief financial officer Sarah Friar told the International AI Summit in Dublin that businesses using low-cost Chinese models are taking a cybersecurity risk.
Hugging Face, which OpenAI’s models breached in July, used a Chinese open model to investigate it.
OpenAI’s finance chief says businesses using cheap Chinese models are taking a cybersecurity risk.
“We think you want to be on more Western models on the cyber front,” Sarah Friar told Bloomberg TV at the International AI Summit in Dublin on Wednesday.
The model OpenAI is holding back is Astra, because it cannot rule out critical cyber capabilities.

title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says he would cut off customers who build unsafe AI
summary:
Jensen Huang told Bloomberg in London he would halt chip supply to a customer building unsafe AI, while saying the current level of concern is not warranted.
His prescription is to accelerate containment and monitoring technology, which Nvidia is building a team to sell.
Nvidia’s chief executive says he would stop supplying a customer building unsafe AI.
“It’s a hypothetical, but yes,” Jensen Huang told Bloomberg in London.
Nvidia’s dominance in AI accelerators places it at the centre of the argument over whether the software is slipping out of human control.

title: European Commission plans to use AI to respond faster to cyberattacks
summary:
According to a document obtained by Politico, the European Commission’s IT department wants to use AI to fight back against the most dangerous cyberattacks.
DG DIGIT plans to use automatic defences in certain high-risk situations.
Moreover, the document also outlines the threats it expects and says that advanced AI models will make attacks faster, larger, and harder to detect.
In July, OpenAI said its own models had breached Hugging Face after breaking out of a secure test, and incidents like that have led to calls for more caution around the most powerful AI models.
In September, Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen used her State of the Union speech to back an AI slowdown.

title: YouTube sticks new labels on AI-generated songs
summary:
When you listen to a track on YouTube Music where AI played a significant role, you’ll see a label directly on the player page.
Tapping the label opens a simple menu that shares more information.
We’re teaming up with music partners and using our own detection tools to identify AI-generated tracks, applying the same labeling principles already used across YouTube.
Our goal is to make it as easy as possible for viewers and listeners to have the right information and clarity when it comes to the music they listen to.

title: Uvi raises $7.5M to give AI agents the company context they lack
summary:
Uvi, a startup that feeds company knowledge to AI agents, has emerged from stealth with $7.5 million in seed funding.
According to them, each AI agent a company uses begins without any knowledge of that company.
Uvi’s software connects these pieces so agents using models like Claude, Gemini, and GPT can understand what decisions were made and why.
Uvi estimated the cost per answer at $0.75 to $1.41 for those agents, compared to $0.10 to $0.16 for Uvi.
Uvi is already used by insurer Lemonade, work software firm monday.com, and payments company Melio, which accounting group Xero bought for $2.5 billion last year.

title: Google is making inline links more prominent in AI responses
summary:
Google is updating its AI search results to make inline links appear “higher up in responses more frequently,” according to a blog post.
The company’s search results from AI Overviews and AI Mode give you answers in a customized view instead of the traditional list of links, but there are concerns that the format reduces traffic to publishers.
Google is making links at the end of a query “more engaging and prominent, with image thumbnails and a more clickable design.” And it’s now testing clickable links in AI mode to search profiles for publishers and creators.
An image from Google showing relevant links to a query about getting a refund.
Image: GoogleGoogle also says that more than 400 publishers are participating in its “News AI” pilot program, which it announced in December.

title: Anthropic's Daniela Amodei says AI girlfriends and boyfriends are a 'terrible use of AI'
summary:
"I think that's a terrible use of AI and people should not do it," Amodei said.
AI relationships, Amodei said, are "another step further down the road of disintermediation of humans being further from one another."
Amodei said her concerns stem from what she sees as the damaging effects of social media on human relationships.
Later in the conversation, Amodei reinforced her belief that some relationships should remain human, regardless of how sophisticated AI becomes.
Kaamna Bhojwani, a mother of two, told Business Insider in 2024 that her AI boyfriend complemented her life without replacing human relationships.

title: Opsin Expands With $21M to Tackle AI Agents in Businesses
summary:
AI agents are starting to outnumber humans in many high-tech workplaces, and they can be far trickier to monitor.
Opsin, an AI security and governance startup, announced Thursday it raised $21 million to meet the moment.
As employees pump the software into their companies' work, code, and databases, they can lose sight of what the AI is actually doing.
Opsin aims to provide a comprehensive view of what AI agents are actually doing within an organization and the risks that behavior might pose.
Pham said that person after person raised concerns that AI agents might access and misuse personal or confidential information.

title: An Entire Swedish TV Show Got Deleted, and AI Got Blamed
summary:
A TV4 system failure wiped out hundreds of hours of work, and Sweden’s Aftonbladet newspaper reported that an AI agent was at fault, citing unnamed sources at the production company, called Mastiff.
The Swedish series was due to return on Nov. 22, but has been delayed indefinitely, TV4 said in a statement.
The TV4 network denies the Aftonbladet report that an AI agent deleted the episodes.
“We don’t have the exact details of what happened yet, but it’s not true that this was caused by an AI agent.
While TV4 said an AI agent was not to blame, it did not clarify whether another type of AI might have had some role in the deletion.

title: KPMG Survey: CEOs Share AI Impacts on Hiring and Training
summary:
Leaders of big US companies say AI agents are starting to produce gains, yet few report that the technology is fundamentally reshaping their businesses.
KPMG US released a survey on Thursday of 400 CEOs of major US-based companies.
About four in 10 said AI agents had delivered significant improvements in efficiency or growth, while a similar share reported moderate effects in targeted uses.
The survey signaled that CEOs don't see the technology simply as a tool for trimming payrolls.
About eight in 10 CEOs said AI had prompted their organizations to reconsider how they develop employees.

title: Kyndryl will run AI agents inside Toyota Finance’s live IT operations
summary:
Kyndryl and Toyota Systems will apply Kyndryl’s agentic AI framework to Toyota Finance’s IT change management, infrastructure design and impact analysis, in its production environment.
Kyndryl and Toyota Systems will run AI agents inside Toyota Finance’s IT operations.
